question: Can a coefficient-independent bounded-precision q-multiple depth proxy select rational two-image lifts whose short public relations have greater exact p-adic depth on fresh targets?
generator_law: first finite point by ascending x then y whose cofactor multiple has exact prime order q
query_law: first 16 lexicographic ordered distinct offsets with both U=Q-t1G and V=Q-t2G nonidentity
distinct_x_candidates: center both points; enumerate shifts of x1,y1,x2,y2 by shift times p; interpolate A=(f1-f2)/(x1-x2), B=f1-Ax1
equal_x_exception: when U,V are distinct opposite points with equal x, use centered P=(x,y), R=(x,-y), A=-1, B=y^2-x^3+x; count one attempt
proxy_law: on each candidate rational model over Qp(p,prec=8), compute qP1 and qP2, then k_i=min(v_p(-x(qP_i)/y(qP_i)),4); exact identity gets cap 4
selection_rule: before coefficient relation outcomes, maximize k1+k2; break ties by minimum full model score then lexicographic shift
baseline_rule: minimum full model score then lexicographic shift
model_score_bits: maximum numerator or denominator bit length of A,B,x1,y1,x2,y2
residual_depth: for each frozen public-hit vector, evaluate exact R=aP1+bP2 over Q; identity is exact relation, otherwise k=v_p(-x(R)/y(R))
controls: verify finite public relation, rational model and point reduction, P1+(-P1)=O, and qP_i reduction to identity; preserve candidate failures
claim_boundary: the q-multiple proxy uses only public subgroup order and candidate lifts; raw vector outcomes are evaluated after selection; this fresh-target panel is an algorithmic diagnostic and not a same-target speedup
